entries.title: Man, 40, fatally shot leaving Grand Crossing gas station Saturday
entries.summary: <p>A 40-year-old man was fatally shot early Saturday by someone who approached him as he left a gas station in Grand Crossing, Chicago police said.</p><p>Police said the shooting took place along the 7100 block of South Vincennes Avenue at about 4:48 a.m.</p><p>The unidentified victim suffered multiple gunshot wounds and was taken to the University of Chicago Medical Center, where he was pronounced dead, police said.</p><p>Police said the alleged shooter fled in a dark SUV. Area 1 detectives are investigating.</p>

entries.title: Mark Scheifele's huge game exposes Blackhawks' lack of shutdown forward
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> have had no answers for Jets star Mark Scheifele for years, and they had none again Saturday.</p><p>A heroic effort by Scheifele rallied the Jets from a four-goal deficit to a 5-4 shootout victory, extending their voodoo-filled winning streak to six games and dealing the Hawks their 10th loss in their last 12.</p><p>Scheifele scored the Jets’ first goal, then took advantage of Hawks goalie Spencer Knight’s stick getting stuck in the boards — a very unlucky break — to set up Kyle Connor to cut the deficit to 4-2 by the second intermission.</p><p>Early in the third, Scheifele deftly tossed the puck into the crease to enable a power-play goal by Cole Perfetti. Late in the third, he showed great vision and sense of timing to hit Gabriel Vilardi in the crease for the tying goal. And in the shootout, he sniped the corner over Knight to convert his attempt.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Jets goal: Gabriel Vilardi with a late goal to tie it. <a href="https://t.co/SCW9xLMrZN">pic.twitter.com/SCW9xLMrZN</a></p>— BHF (@BlackhawksFocus) <a href="https://x.com/BlackhawksFocus/status/2121742123963760725?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 14, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>It was an MVP-caliber, four-point performance. From a Hawks perspective, however, it wasn’t anything they hadn’t seen before.</p><p>Scheifele now has 46 points in 51 career games against the Hawks, including a whopping 14 in their last six meetings. Many of those have come in clutch fashion, too.</p><p>In October 2024, he scored with 64 seconds left in regulation and again 38 seconds into overtime to flip a 1-0 Hawks lead into a 2-1 Jets victory.</p><p>In March 2026, he assisted on a goal with 39 seconds left in regulation and scored two minutes into overtime to flip a 2-1 Hawks lead into a 3-2 Jets victory.</p><p>Despite seeing it over and over, the Hawks can’t seem to stop it. Anecdotes such as those reiterate just how desperately they lack a true shutdown forward capable of stifling opposing stars on a nightly basis.</p><p>Granted, they also lack a reliable six-man defensive corps — although Alex Vlasic and Ian Cole were excellent Saturday — and a second offensive star to complement Connor Bedard, among many other things. Their holes are plentiful.</p><p>Obviously, a Selke Trophy-caliber center would transform the Hawks’ lineup, but those types of players are rare. The Hawks are trying to develop their own in Anton Frondell, whom they believe might become their next Jonathan Toews. That’s why they’re stubbornly <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/13/how-blackhawks-rookie-anton-frondell-keeps-friendship-alive-with-jets-rookie-viggo-bjorck" target="_blank" >keeping him at center</a> instead of moving him to Bedard’s wing.</p><p>But even somebody such as former Hawks forward Jason Dickinson would make a big difference. Although Dickinson’s game was one-dimensional and he contributed little offense, he could — and, with the Oilers, still can — shut down opponents at an elite level.</p><p>Dickinson was also a critical component of the Hawks’ penalty kill and six-on-five defense, which is notable, considering the events of Saturday.</p><p>He wasn’t great on faceoffs, but he was respectable. The Hawks, who won only 19 of 60 draws Saturday and rank last in the NHL in faceoff winning percentage by a wide margin, could use that, too.</p><p>I wrote two games into this season how the Hawks seemed to be missing the stability Dickinson, Ilya Mikheyev and Connor Murphy provided, and I’ve had that same thought countless times since then.</p><p>Those veterans kept the team afloat in the defensive zone perhaps more than anyone appreciated at the time. They also made it a no-brainer decision for Hawks coaches about which line and defensive pairing would handle the toughest matchups in every game.</p><p>Without their services this season, coach Jeff Blashill has shifted around those responsibilities on a game-to-game basis, and he hasn’t found a consistent formula.</p><p>It was strange that Frondell, who did a good job in a heavy matchup role against Scheifele on Oct. 15, barely saw Scheifele on Saturday. Instead, Bedard’s line received the most ice time against Scheifele, and an injury to Tyler Bertuzzi in the third period further tilted the Hawks’ disadvantage in that matchup.</p>

entries.title: Bulls see travel squeeze in wake of longest ground stoppage in 25 years
entries.summary: <p>MINNEAPOLIS – The longest nationwide ground stoppage in 25 years impacted the flight plans of the entire country in the last 48 hours.</p><p>The Bulls were no exceptions to that.</p><p>Scheduled to leave Chicago after their Friday win against Atlanta and head to the Twin Cities for a back-to-back with Minnesota, the team found out afterwards that they would instead leave Saturday morning. Even that was delayed slightly, however, with the team getting in around noon.</p><p>Luckily, because it was a back-to-back it didn’t alter a ton of game preparation. In the normal second game of a back-to-back, teams often have no morning shootaround, instead watching film at the hotel and possibly going through a mock walkthrough in a hotel ballroom.</p><p>Bulls coach Tiago Splitter simply pushed the schedule to pre-game at the arena. The team had a film session 35 minutes before tip-off and went through strategy at that time.</p><p>It was still a first for Splitter, however.</p><p>“It’s kind of weird to travel the morning of a game,” he said. “At least for me it’s a first.”</p><p>What Splitter made sure of was his team didn’t use it as an excuse, especially because dozens of teams across the NBA, NFL and college football had to deal with the travel issues.</p><p>“Other than that it’s a back-to-back,” Splitter added. “You gotta bring the energy. Your legs are going to be a little heavier than normal but just take it like another game.”</p><p>As far as the rest of the three-city trip, it was business as usual. The Bulls were expected to fly to Cleveland Sunday afternoon and have the usual morning shootaround in preparation for the Monday night game with the Cavaliers.</p><p></p><p><b>Staying the course</b></p><p></p><p>It would have been easy for splinters to start coming to the surface in the locker room with the dismal 1-9 start, but as the win over the Hawks showed the locker room remains patient with the process.</p><p>“We’re doing a good job of that,” veteran Jalen Smith said when asked if the locker room showed any chemistry rough patches. “We’re a young team, we’re really connected with one another, you know. Pretty much everyone is around the same age, give or take a few guys, so we have a great relationship. We knew it was going to be hard – whole new front office, whole new coaching staff – we just got to put together wins. The NBA is a big boys’ league, you lose, you lose, but you want to go out fighting.</p><p>“I think we’re making the right strides. Everyone is trusting the process, everyone is putting in extra work, watching film, making sure we’re correcting our mistakes.”</p><p></p><p><b>The training room</b></p><p></p><p>Smith (left finger sprain) was injured late in the overtime win over Atlanta and wasn’t able to go on Saturday. The good news was it seemed like a minor setback rather than anything long term, according to the center.</p><p>As far as Nic Claxton and how the Bulls are going to handle playing him in back-to-backs after he missed the first three weeks of the season with a tweaked hamstring? They’re not. For the time being he will not play in the second game of a back-to-back.</p><p></p><p><b>Where’s Lenny?</b></p><p></p><p>Leonard Miller was one of the few positive surprises late last season and seemed to be capitalizing on that momentum throughout the summer and into the preseason, but after a subpar start to his season, he’s currently out of the rotation for the time being.</p><p>Shooting 18.5% and 43.4% from the field didn’t help.</p><p>“He had an outstanding summer for us, preseason,” Splitter said. “Now he’s a little bit out of the rotation. He didn’t start the season the way he wanted, but hopefully he can bounce back and play the way he was during the summer.”</p>

entries.title: Cancellations, delays at O'Hare, Midway continue Saturday in fallout from FAA ground stop

Federal officials said travel should be back to normal by Sunday.</p><p>For United passenger Abdul Sankoh of Manassas, Virginia, the disruption meant spending more than seven hours aboard a plane stuck on the tarmac, missing his scheduled arrival at Dulles International Airport in Washington, D.C., and spending another four hours Saturday morning waiting in line to speak with an airline customer service representative.</p><p>Sankoh had been scheduled to depart O'Hare Airport for Dulles at 2:21 p.m. Friday. entries.title: Cary-Grove forces four turnovers, rushes for 431 yards to beat St. Francis
entries.summary: <p>In Cary and Fox River Grove, kids grow up counting the days till they can suit up in Penn State-inspired navy-blue-and-white uniforms to play on a pristine grass football field with old-school goalposts.</p><p>Junior lineman Caleb Wright was one of those kids hoping to add to Cary-Grove’s tradition.</p><p>‘‘It’s like nothing else, if I’m being honest,’’ Wright said. ‘‘We all dreamed about this before we go to sleep, and it’s all seeming to come true now. We’ve just got to keep executing, getting better every single day.’’</p><p>The No. 25 Trojans have another week to get better after turning four takeaways into 27 points and knocking out defending champion St. Francis 55-36 in a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2026/10/17/ihsa-state-football-playoff-pairings-class5a-illinois-2026" target="_blank" >Class 5A</a> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/scores/2026/11/13/2026-ihsa-state-football-quarterfinal-playoff-scores" target="_blank" >quarterfinal</a> Saturday in Cary.</p><p>Cary-Grove (10-2) will host Sycamore (9-4) next weekend in search of its fourth state-championship berth since 2018.</p><p>‘‘For many years, the semifinals were the standard here,’’ Trojans coach Brad Seaburg said. ‘‘And now that standard has really been elevated. And so the kids know that, yeah, the semifinals is where we want to be right now. But we want to keep going.’’</p><p>Thanks to a big first half by the defense, they will.</p><p>Junior Zach Witt had two interceptions, and sophomore Leo Zavala picked off a pass and recovered a fumble forced by Wright.</p><p>‘‘Our game plan was just play as a team and just not try to be a hero,’’ Witt said. ‘‘We had our D-line having great pressure, our linebackers filling holes, our corners really going after those wide receivers all night.’’</p><p>The turnovers and takeaways were unusual for both teams, Seaburg noted.</p><p>‘‘We have not [been creating turnovers], and they have not turned the ball over like that all year,’’ Seaburg said. ‘‘So we did some things to them that [caused them to do things] they haven’t been doing all year. . . . I think that’s a testament to our defense.’’</p><p>‘‘I give a lot of credit to those coaches and those kids,’’ St. Francis coach Bob McMillen said. ‘‘They literally beat the crap out of us. And you can’t turn the ball over four times against a team like that.’’</p><p>This was as inexperienced a team as Seaburg has had in his 16 seasons. The Trojans had to replace four starters on the offensive line and both tight ends — all key cogs in their triple-option attack.</p><p>But they did have one key player with experience back: junior quarterback Jackson Berndt.</p><p>‘‘He’s got two years of varsity experience,’’ Seaburg said. ‘‘And as a freshman, he took quite a few snaps in the playoffs. He’s a cool cat back there. Very composed.’’</p><p>Berndt ran 11 times for 124 yards and a touchdown. Senior Shamarion Prude had 13 carries for 170 yards and a touchdown, and sophomore Luke Ceresa ran nine times for 59 yards and three scores.</p><p>‘‘We just have a rotation going,’’ Ceresa said. ‘‘ ‘Sham’ and I, we switch every three [plays]. . . . I think we complement each other great, and the offensive line just had a great push on all the runs.’’</p><p>Berndt threw one pass, which fell incomplete, and Cary-Grove ran 42 times for 431 yards. The Trojans led 34-14 at halftime and 41-14 midway through the third quarter.</p><p>For St. Francis (7-6), junior quarterback Jadon Wilson was 16-for-28 for 230 yards and four touchdowns — two each to Blayke Lohmann and Noah Turner — with three interceptions and a lost fumble. He also ran 16 times for 92 yards.</p><p>Tivias Caldwell Jr. had 25 carries for 127 yards and a touchdown for the Spartans.</p>

entries.title: Notre Dame has no trouble with visiting Boston College
entries.summary: <p>SOUTH BEND, Ind. — CJ Carr passed for 217 yards and two touchdowns, and No. 3 Notre Dame showed no letdown after knocking off Miami last week, beating Boston College 41-7 on Saturday.</p><p>Notre Dame beat then-No. 1 Miami 31-24 last Saturday. The Fighting Irish (9-1), who are No. 5 in the College Football Playoff rankings, returned Saturday and rolled to a 31-0 halftime lead.</p><p>Fighting Irish coach Marcus Freeman said his team did a great job of blocking out noise all week about 1993, when Notre Dame beat No. 1 Florida State but then lost to Boston College at home the next week.</p><p>“I thought the leadership was spot on this week, and I thought the guys understood the challenge they had in front of us, and they went out and played that way,” Freeman said. “I think you can look at the product that you saw on the field today and say they prepared the right way, they had the right mindset, but I think every day it’s a choice. It’s a choice you make.”</p><p>Carr completed 20-of-28 passes, including a 26-yard TD pass to Micah Gilbert and a 13-yard scoring strike to Jordan Faison. He praised the team's focus against Boston College after the Miami victory.</p><p>“We try and do this with losses a lot, but what can we take from that game against Miami into this next week. You want to flush the feelings and the urge to stay in ... that moment," Carr said. "I think we can take the detail and the preparation that we had from that week and use that to propel us into this week and weeks beyond.”</p><p>Freshman running back Jonaz Walton gained 141 yards on 15 carries and scored on a 1-yard run. Nolan James Jr. added 73 yards rushing and a 10-yard TD. They replaced NFL first-round picks Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price.</p><p>“They’re just continuously getting better,” Freeman said. “They’re continuously working together. They’re seeing things that maybe they didn’t see a month ago or two months ago.”</p><p>Jaylen Sneed scored a 1-yard scoop-and-score touchdown off a fumble forced by Boubacar Traore. The Fighting Irish limited Boston College to 136 yards of total offense.</p><p>Boston College (4-6) cashed in on Carr’s second interception of the season. K.P. Price picked off the pass at the Notre Dame 27. Three plays later, the Eagles’ Bo MacCormack III powered into the end zone from the 3 for the touchdown.</p><p><b>The Takeaway</b></p><p>Defense opened the door for a 24-0 domination by Notre Dame in the second quarter. Boston College had minus-10 yards of total offense in the second quarter.</p><p>Boston College added to its Atlantic Coast Conference-best mark for interceptions when Price intercepted Carr's pass. The Eagles lead the ACC with 13 interceptions. Price has four.</p><p><b>Up next</b></p><p>Boston College: Hosts Syracuse next Saturday.</p><p>Notre Dame: Hosts SMU next Saturday.</p>

entries.title: Man, 21, dies after paraglider crashes in Plainfield
entries.summary: <p>A 21-year-old man died Saturday after his paraglider crashed into a farm field in Plainfield following an apparent in-flight emergency, police said.</p><p>Police received a call at 2:57 p.m. about the crash that occurred near 127th Street and Ridge Road, according to a news release.</p><p>Witnesses at the scene assisted the pilot until Oswego paramedics arrived and attempted lifesaving measures, police said.</p><p>Giovanni Lopez, of Woodridge, was pronounced dead at the scene by the Kendall County coroner's office, police said.</p><p>Plainfield police detectives and the Kendall County coroner's office are investigating.</p>

entries.title: Life without Caleb Wilson carries on for Bulls, evident by a second win
entries.summary: <p>MINNEAPOLIS – There’s a next-man-up mentality that most professional franchises need to have.</p><p>At least the ones that have any hopes of surviving a significant injury to the roster.</p><p>The Bulls displayed that in the wake of prized rookie Caleb Wilson being lost for up to six weeks because of undergoing right hand surgery, beating Atlanta in overtime on Friday and showing up a night later with by far their best basketball of the season in upsetting the Timberwolves 117-106.</p><p>Not a bad response at all.</p><p>“Our jobs are on the line too,” reserve guard Buddy Hield said very matter-of-factly after the latest win. “The organization is in the position where they’re trying to figure out where they are moving in the next direction. No disrespect to Caleb, but we have guys that have been in the league for more than four or five years and we understand what it takes to win. Putting all the BS aside and being a good teammate, going out to compete, making winning plays and that translates into wins.”</p><p>Words that followed up actions from Hield, as it was the likes of him, Patrick Williams and Tre Jones that came off the bench, withstood a third-quarter rally by the home team, and helped the Bulls to a 3-9 record.</p><p>Hield and Jones each had 16 points, while Williams added 15 points and was a plus-10 in plus/minus.</p><p>“We’re winners,” Williams said of the bench mentality. “That’s what winners do. Do whatever you need to when your name is called. Whatever it looks like, whether it’s scoring, rebounding, whatever it is.”</p><p>That was the latest known for the Bulls.</p><p>The unknown is how will the 20-year-old Wilson handle being a spectator and not a key foundation piece until possibly Christmas time?</p><p>If it’s up to the Bulls, it won’t be him overthinking the setback on his own.</p><p>Coach Tiago Splitter went into a bit more detail on Saturday about the plan surrounding Wilson and how the organization wants to handle his rehabilitation. It involves being around the team as much as possible, likely starting after this three-city road trip.</p><p>“He’s not traveling right now because he still has stitches and he can’t sweat yet, so a couple days off, but once we come back (from this road trip) he’s going to be around the team and travel with the team,” the coach said.</p><p>Which Splitter, the medical staff and the front office all deem key in his comeback.</p><p>“I think it’s extremely important just to be a part of the film sessions, the meetings, be on the bench, be part of the goods and bads of the team throughout those games,” Splitter said. “It’s also going to give him a different perspective on not having the pressure of the game and the open mind to just watch everything, try to learn and absorb everything from those situations.”</p><p>Considering the Bulls were near the bottom of the league in offensive efficiency and at the bottom in defense, it’s not like life without Wilson would do damage to either of those statistical categories.</p><p>The two major gut-punches specifically center around Wilson.</p><p>First and foremost, it’s a month to six weeks of development that every rookie needs, especially one that was being counted on as heavily as Wilson was. The other slap is Wilson’s Rookie of the Year candidacy and how important it was to him.</p><p>Since first being drafted back in June, Wilson has not been shy in admitting that he not only wanted to win the Rookie of the Year trophy of a very talented 2026 draft but wanted to personally outperform any rookie in the class whenever he faced them.</p><p>This setback puts him near the back of the line behind the likes of Cameron Boozer, Darius Acuff Jr., Yaxel Lendeborg, Darryn Peterson and AJ Dybantsa.</p>

entries.title: Dear Abby: Wedding invitation leads to unpleasant breakup
entries.summary: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> I dated a man for 16 months. We spent a lot of time together. We traveled, enjoyed many sports events and shared some mutual friends who actually introduced us.</p><p>One evening, we were out for dinner with another couple of his friends. During the conversation, the woman asked him if I was going to his daughter's wedding. His response shocked me. He shook his head, saying, "I don't think so." I remained calm, but I felt hurt. It wasn't because I "had" to go to the wedding but because he didn't even discuss it with me.</p><p>I was embarrassed, so I excused myself from the table. When I returned, I asked for my jacket. His response was, "This isn't going to end well." I asked him if that was a threat, to which he did not respond. I called a ride share and left.</p><p>The next day, he delivered all my belongings from his apartment. Over — just like that! No explanation. He did scream at me while dropping off my things, about why I thought I should be invited when I had never met his daughter. I couldn't speak at the time because I was dumbfounded. A few days later, we had a text exchange. I asked him about a golfing buddy of his being invited. He said yes. I said, "He never met your daughter." Phone silence.</p><p>He later invited me to go to lunch but said, "No crying." I declined and said, "I don't want to eat, and I don't want to be friends with someone who treats me so horribly." A week or two later, I got an email saying, "This is my last communication ever." I don't think he had to announce it, but OK. It's been a year now, but it still bothers me. Am I wrong? — <i>MAKING NO SENSE IN MINNESOTA</i></p><p><b>DEAR MAKING NO SENSE:</b> The man you were dating had his reasons for not inviting the woman he had been seeing for 16 months. If I had been sitting in your position, rather than pouting and retreating, I would have asked him why he hadn't mentioned such an important milestone and let him explain it in front of his friends. That said, the romance is over. Let it go. To say that he was controlling and insensitive would be an understatement. In my opinion, you dodged a nasty bullet.</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> I belong to a group of 10 women who meet once a month. We're all seniors, and most, but not all, of the women have husbands. I'd like to set up a dinner for couples so we can meet each other's husbands. Should I invite only those with spouses? Invite everyone, but ask that the singles bring a date? Just let the singles come solo? — <i>HESITANT HOSTESS</i></p><p><b>DEAR HOSTESS:</b> Why would you need to exclude the single women as you meet one another's husbands? I suspect they, too, are curious about their friends' spouses. Make sure the singles know they are welcome to bring a date if they want to, but they, not you, should decide whether mingling with a roomful of couples will make them uncomfortable.</p><p>Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127. </p>

entries.title: Lt. Gov.-elect Christian Mitchell blazes new Illinois trail: 'I realize whose shoulders I stand on'
entries.summary: <p>Democrats’ blue tsunami on election night ushered in a wave of “firsts” across the nation, from the first Black woman elected governor, Georgia’s Keisha Lance Bottoms, to the first Muslim person elected to the U.S. Senate, Michigan’s Abdul El-Sayed.</p><p>It also washed over Illinois, which will become the first state <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/11/04/juliana-strattons-win-marks-historic-first-for-women-of-color-in-national-politics" target="_blank" ><u>to send two women of color to the U.S. Senate</u></a> when outgoing Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton is sworn in alongside incumbent Sen. Tammy Duckworth in January.</p><p>Stratton’s ascent allowed for another new trail to be blazed in her office, which will be filled by Christian Mitchell, the first Black man elected as Illinois’ lieutenant governor.</p><p>“I feel incredibly honored by it,” Mitchell told the Sun-Times. “I realize whose shoulders I stand on. I realize we lost Jesse Jackson this year, who talked about keeping hope alive and did so much work for the vote, and John Lewis, and so many people.”</p><p>But first on the 40-year-old former legislator’s mind, while addressing a packed Navy Pier ballroom after declaring <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/11/03/governor-illinois-jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-collin-corbett-results" target="_blank" ><u>victory alongside Gov. JB Pritzker</u></a>, were his mother, Deb Gist; his late grandmother, Lilly Mae Gist; and his late grandfather and “hero,” James Gist, who served as a U.S. Army sergeant.</p><p>“At the time he went out to fight for this country in Korea, we did not have the Civil Rights Act, and he did not have his rights of the franchise guaranteed. So on a personal level, I feel that weight,” Mitchell said the day after making history.</p><p>“Juliana blazed a trail here as the first Black woman to be lieutenant governor. The fact that we have so many of these firsts in 2026 shows that we still have a ways to go, so I’m very grateful,” he said. “But we have so much more work to do, and ultimately, regardless of your color, your creed, where you live, I want to be a lieutenant governor for everyone in the way that JB has been a governor for everybody.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div no defined responsibilities beyond being a heartbeat away from becoming governor, Mitchell’s position as lieutenant governor-elect takes on enhanced significance as Pritzker considers running for president.</p><p>Mitchell’s job description will shift considerably if the third-term governor hits the 2028 campaign trail — and he’ll make even more history if Pritzker actually wins the White House.</p><p>Mitchell says that hasn’t affected the way he approaches the office, and the prospect of becoming the state’s first Black governor is not what drew him back to public service after a two-year stint as vice president of civic engagement at the University of Chicago.</p><p>“I've always said and always been taught by my mentors, including JB, that if you do the job that you have in front of you, the future takes care of itself,” Mitchell said, hardly downplaying Pritzker’s potential national ambition.</p><p>“It's good that people look at that and say, ‘Hey, with everything broken in Washington, we want that kind of leadership to go national.’ That's great,” Mitchell said. “It's also why it's great that he won a third term. So for me, as his governing partner and somebody who every day approaches his job with a high level of seriousness and a focus on the kind of people who raised me — single moms, union workers, farmers — I'm going to do that, no matter what's potentially happening.</p><p>“And ultimately it's why I'm so glad to be running with somebody who said, ‘Hey, I want to do this again, I want to run for a third term.’ I want to keep the work going,” said Mitchell, who has been one of Pritzker’s closest confidants since the governor was first elected in 2018.</p><p>The Bronzeville resident became the youngest state representative at the time he was elected from the 26th District in 2012 at age 26, serving three terms before being named a deputy governor in Pritzker’s administration in 2019.</p><p>Mitchell shepherded Pritzker’s signature $45 billion capital infrastructure program through the General Assembly and ran point on other key legislation, including landmark climate legislation aiming to wean Illinois off fossil fuels.</p><p>Mitchell, a former adviser to Cook County Board President Toni Preckwinkle, also helped manage the rollout of the state’s recreational cannabis industry, while leading <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/opinion/2020/7/3/21312061/coronavirus-illinois-medical-supplies-wild-west-competition-face-masks-christian-mitchell-stockpiles" target="_blank" ><u>frenzied procurement efforts</u></a> for badly needed supplies in the darkest early days of the COVID-19 pandemic.</p><p>An Illinois Air National Guard first lieutenant by part-time trade and an amateur boxer by hobby, Mitchell says he’s excited to get back to the Capitol.</p><p>“Getting out on the trail was really the most invigorating for me,” he said. “The challenges are common, but so are the hopes, so is the decency. I'm a Black man from the South Side of Chicago, and I'm going to places where often people don't look like me, and I still felt incredibly welcome.</p><p>“In the state, if you get it right and you can convince colleagues to do it, you can move pretty quickly... You can do things pretty quickly if you pull the right people together.”</p>

entries.title: Analyzing Blackhawks defenseman Sam Rinzel's play at his personal 82-game mark
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> defenseman <b>Sam Rinzel</b> talks a lot about playing to strengths — his strength being his play in the offensive zone — and finally is starting to make hay from that.</p><p>Unfortunately for the Hawks, Rinzel’s weakness — playing in the defensive zone — continues to be problematic.</p><p>Coach <b>Jeff Blashill</b> called the Jets’ two goals late in the second period the turning point of the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/14/blackhawks-jets-mark-scheifele-shutdown-forward-jason-dickinson" target="_blank" >Hawks’ loss Saturday</a>. Considering the second was a fluke, the first is worth analyzing closely.</p><p>Leading up to it, the Jets’ <b>Mark Scheifele</b>, <b>Kyle Connor</b>, <b>Viggo Bjorck</b> and <b>Josh Morrissey</b> went to work in the left corner of the Hawks’ defensive zone, executing a smooth cycle play that ended with Morrissey finding Scheifele in front of the net.</p><p><b>Connor Bedard</b> deserves some of the blame as the low center. Bedard moved away from the net a few seconds before the goal to cut off Morrissey’s lane for a potential seam pass to <b>Mario Ferraro</b> on the far side, and he was too slow to reassess the play and return to Scheifele.</p><p>But the whole sequence took place in Rinzel’s corner, which he didn’t control assertively enough. He looked torn about whether to be aggressive or passive and mostly opted for passiveness. When he finally chose to pressure Morrissey, he was a half-second late, and his stick wasn’t in position to disrupt the pass.</p><p>It’s another lesson for Rinzel. He said earlier this season he thinks many people — including himself sometimes — tend to forget how inexperienced he is, and that’s true.</p><p>Saturday was his 82nd career NHL game, meaning he just now has played the equivalent of a full season. The fact that those games have been spread over three real-life seasons distorts perception.</p><p>But that doesn’t excuse the frequency of the defensive-zone turnovers, failed breakouts and minor penalties that have plagued him this season. The Hawks need better from him in his own zone.</p><h3>Rinzel’s offensive growth</h3><p>Still, Rinzel recently has shown more flashes of the offensively dynamic version of himself Hawks fans briefly saw when he made his NHL debut in April 2025.</p><p>He picked up two assists Saturday — both on the power play, which he’s quarterbacking right now — to give him seven in his last seven games. His nine points this season lead Hawks defensemen.</p><p>He didn’t get an assist but also deserved kudos for an accurate breakout pass from the defensive zone to <b>Tyler Bertuzzi</b> in the first period. That jump-started a rush on which Bertuzzi scored.</p><p>‘‘Overall, I think he’s had real good progress over the last couple of weeks,’’ Blashill said Thursday. ‘‘He just has to stay with that kind of progress.’’</p><h3>Kaiser’s highs and lows</h3><p>Fellow defenseman <b>Wyatt Kaiser</b> has been on the ice for 28 five-on-five goals against this season, the most in the league. It’s an ugly stat that reflects how low his lows have been.</p><p>His highs are still high, however. His shifty skating style and creative mind give him the potential to be a difference-maker when he’s on his A-game.</p><p>The problem lately has been his ratio of good games to bad games. He strung some good ones together in October, but November has been less consistent.</p><p>In the first period Saturday, for example, he committed a bad turnover in the defensive zone on one shift, then executed an impressive solo breakout just a couple of shifts later.</p><p>‘‘He’s always hypercompetitive,’’ Blashill said Saturday. ‘‘When he’s efficient with the puck is when he’s at his best. . . . And staying away from big errors defensively.’’</p>

entries.title: Delays, cancellations dropping at Chicago's airports following Friday's ground stop
entries.summary: <p>Fewer delays and cancellations at Chicago's airports were reported so far on Sunday following Friday's nationwide ground stop.</p><p>As of late morning Sunday morning, O'Hare International Airport was reporting 272 delayed flights and 145 canceled flights, according to the flight tracking website FlightAware. That's a considerable drop from Saturday when the airport experienced 894 delays and 742 cancellations.</p><p>Midway International Airport saw similar improvement, according to FlightAware's data. As of Sunday morning, the airport had 112 delays and 35 cancellations. On Saturday, Midway reported 143 delayed flights and 76 canceled flights.</p><p>Air travel was thrown into chaos across the country Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare, nationwide ground stop. <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/transportation/2026/11/13/all-departing-flights-grounded-nationwide-due-to-faa-order" target="_blank" >Federal officials blamed</a> the country's aging air traffic control system for instability in air traffic control communications.</p>

entries.title: Patrick Williams following a Buddy system and helping the Bulls lately
entries.summary: <p>MINNEAPOLIS — At times it seems like Buddy Hield is from a different planet and everyone else is just visiting it.</p><p>The veteran <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls" >Bulls</a> shooter is always smiling, always talking, and every so often breaking off in some sort of happy dance where he appears to be skipping down the bench area.</p><p>“A good vibes guy” is how coach Tiago Splitter describes his veteran reserve. A better compliment in Hield’s eyes? Just call him a “professional.”</p><p>That was on full display over the last week alone as Hield went from rotation guy at the start of the season to slowly being phased out, picking up two DNPs (Did Not Play) Coach’s Decision in recent losses to Philadelphia and San Antonio.</p><p>No problem, as he put in 25-plus minutes in the overtime win against Atlanta on Friday night and then followed that up with 16 points and a plus-11 in plus/minus in a massive win over Minnesota. Just how big of a shocker was the win for Hield and the Bulls? It was the biggest upset in 35 years for a team a 16.5-point underdog.</p><p>Hield, however, was acting like it was just another day at the office.</p><p>“You got to be professional, man, treat this like a job,” Hield said of his mindset. “Even when you don’t play, be the best teammate you can be. Just find ways to contribute.</p><p>“Once you start stacking up a few wins in this league, this (bleep) continues and that’s what we’re trying to do. My job is to be the best veteran leader that I can be to help these guys to stay composed, don’t get too high, don’t get too low. It’s tough to win in this league and when you’re losing teams bury you, they don’t feel sorry for you.”</p><p>Patrick Williams knows that all too well. The former No. 4 overall pick has gone from promise to bust to not even an afterthought in recent years, starting the season collecting $18 million per year and not even getting on the court.</p><p>Williams missed the first seven games, finally getting mop-up duty in New York, but has suddenly emerged into a 20-plus minutes guy the last four games. He was stellar against Minnesota, scoring 14 points and grabbing five rebounds, while posting a plus-10.</p><p>“We all know Pat is a great NBA basketball player,” Hield said. “Besides, what happens in the past, you flush that. This league is all about what have you done for me lately and what Pat’s done lately is tremendous, so we’re going to keep building on that.”</p><p>Williams, like Hield, credited just keeping a “professional mindset.”</p><p>“You always have those doubts, no matter who you are,” Williams admitted of his rocky last four seasons. “Whether I was playing 30 minutes or three minutes, you always have those doubts with you as a player. That’s what the work is for. Work kind of relieves some of those doubts, and then giving yourself to the team you don’t have so much time to worry about yourself. Everybody goes through adversity. It’s how you get through it.”</p><p>Maybe that’s why the bench was suddenly feeling better about itself. If Hield and Williams can contribute like they have the last few games, redefining their roles, could that lead to better things for the entire second unit?</p><p>Veteran reserve Tre Jones thinks so.</p><p>“Guys have stepped up big for us,” Jones said of the bench. “Every single night we know as a team that it might be somebody else but we know we can do this together. We got off to a rough start this year, but we also know it’s a long year. We have some guys in here that have a lot of experience and we’re going to lean on that.”</p>

entries.summary: <p>St. Ignatius quarterback Reid Hites finished off Loyola on Saturday by running backward out of his own end zone to intentionally take a safety.</p><p>The smart move to secure the Wolfpack’s 21-18 upset of Loyola in the Class 8A quarterfinals.</p><p>St. Ignatius restarted its football program in 2006 after shutting it down in the mid-1960’s. Since the restart, the program was 0-12 against Loyola and had not beaten the Ramblers since 1952.</p><p>Hites is just a junior, but he’s mastered the triple-option offense along with running backs Luca and Nino Capuano. Hites had 20 carries for 88 yards and two touchdowns against Loyola.</p><p>St. Ignatius lost 38-7 at Loyola in October. But the Wolfpack forced Loyola into multiple mistakes on Saturday and dominated the line of scrimmage.</p><p>Up next for Ignatius is a trip to Northfield for an 8A semifinal game against New Trier.</p><h3>Brother Rice ascends</h3><p>Mount Carmel’s <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2026/11/14/mount-carmel-takes-lincoln-way-easts-best-shot-and-survives-in-class-8a-quarterfinal-classic" >win in Frankfort against undefeated Lincoln-Way East</a> opened up the top spot in the rankings. The Caravan and Brother Rice were the contenders. The Crusaders grab the spot due to their head-to-head win against Mount Carmel in late September.</p><p>Brother Rice’s only loss came at Lincoln-Way East in Week 1, before star freshman Sam Holcomb won the full-time starting quarterback job.</p><p>Oswego and St. Ignatius join the top five, and Coal City makes its season debut at No. 25. The Coalers only loss this season was against Morris. They host the Warriors in the 4A semifinals this weekend.</p><h3>Ring around the rosy?</h3><p>On two plays against Lincoln-Way East, Mount Carmel was up to some pre-snap hijinks. The Caravan players joined hands and danced ring-around-the-rosy style, then ran to the line of scrimmage to snap the ball.</p><p>“We call it rosy,” Caravan wide receiver Duran Sims said. “It’s very fun. We came up with it in the middle of the week, it was random, and we all liked it.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Mount Carmel does the ring around the rosy again. Barely beats the play clock but does get the 1 yard needed for a first down. <a href="https://t.co/Wt7RxCt3BZ">pic.twitter.com/Wt7RxCt3BZ</a></p>— Michael O'Brien (@michaelsobrien) <a href="https://x.com/michaelsobrien/status/2121709255774666895?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 14, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3>More public vs. private</h3><p>It was the final game for retiring Lincoln-Way East coach Rob Zvonar, and the successful public school coach was emotional in his postgame comments to the press. But even under those circumstances, the state’s current hot-button issue was on his mind.</p><p>“To take a group like this, a true team, a true community team…we had our transfers [previously],” Zvonar said. “It is a little different than [Mount Carmel’s] because they actually have to move. This year we didn’t [have transfers]. This group came from three zip codes, unlike their 103. Their all-star team; we took them deep. We didn’t get the job done, and we are upset about that. I could not be more proud of a group of kids. We almost accomplished something amazing… to have one of the better teams in the country on the ropes. entries.title: Lions rout Patriots 35-10 in Munich as both teams suffer injuries
entries.summary: <p>MUNICH — Detroit Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown caught two touchdown passes in his German homecoming and Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and two scores in a 35-10 win over the New England Patriots, who lost quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury on their opening drive Sunday.</p><p>The Lions (7-2) have won five straight games but also lost edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who appeared to hurt his knee while celebrating the sack that knocked Maye out of the game.</p><p>Jared Goff threw three touchdown passes, along with two interceptions, completing 20 of 31 passes for 303 yards.</p><p>St. Brown caught a 56-yard touchdown pass in the first quarter to give Detroit a 7-3 lead. And his 28-yard TD reception — after teammates pushed him over the goal line in a scrum with Patriots defenders — made it 28-3 in the third quarter</p><p>St. Brown, who wore lederhosen for his arrival to the stadium, charged onto the field carrying a German flag. His mother is German and he spent childhood summers visiting the country.</p><p>In between, Goff found Isaac TeSlaa for a 12-yard touchdown pass and a 14-3 lead after a 97-yard drive, and Gibbs ran it in from 5 yards one play after he rumbled down the sideline for a 50-yard reception.</p><p>Gibbs added a 28-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter to make it 35-10. He is the first NFL player since Priest Holmes in 2002 to produce more than 150 yards rushing with two rushing touchdowns and at least 95 yards receiving in a game, the Lions said.</p><p>Gibbs caught seven passes for 99 yards. St. Brown finished with four receptions for 98 yards.</p><p>The Patriots (5-5) have lost back-to-back games and three of their past four.</p><p>Tommy DeVito completed 12 of 24 for 81 yards with one interception and a fourth-quarter touchdown pass to Lan Larison for New England.</p><p>On his only drive, Maye completed three of four passes for 48 yards. He also scrambled for 11 yards. Hutchinson sacked Maye at the Detroit 15-yard line on third down. Andy Borregales then kicked a 33-yard field goal.</p><p>After DeVito entered the game, the Patriots punted on four straight possessions. DeVito then threw an interception to Roger McCreary late in the first half. The Lions couldn't capitalize, though. Goff was picked off in the back of the end zone by Kevin Byard III.</p><p>Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez had his first interception of the season in the first half. Mack Hollins led the Patriots with five catches for 48 yards.</p><h3>New field incoming</h3><h3></h3><p>Immediately after the game, workers will start installing a new field. Bayern Munich hosts Cologne on Friday night in a Bundesliga game. The NFL wouldn't confirm a German media report that said the league would pay up to 200,000 euros ($220,000) for the new pitch. In a statement to AP, the league said only that it will "work in partnership with Allianz Arena to replace the field following Sunday's game."</p><h3>Injuries</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Patriots:</b> Besides Maye, WR A.J. Brown left in the second half with a hamstring injury. Brown had missed the past two games with ankle and knee problems... RT Morgan Moses left in the first quarter but returned before halftime ... RB TreVeyon Henderson, who didn't make the trip, was placed on injured reserve Saturday.</p><p><b>Lions:</b> Hutchinson left in the first quarter and was later ruled out.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Patriots:</b> Bye week.</p><p><b>Lions:</b> Host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers next Sunday.<br></p>

entries.title: UChicago, U of I students selected as Rhodes Scholar recipients in 2027
entries.summary: <p>Two Illinois college students were selected for the 2027 Rhodes Scholar program.</p><p>The students, seniors from the University of Chicago and University of Illinois at Champaign-Urbana, are among the 32 Americans selected for the prestigious scholarship program in England. The scholars begin fully funded postgraduate programs at the University of Oxford in October 2027.</p><p>Almoatasim M.N. Shahbain, from Burr Ridge, is studying political science at the University of Illinois. Shahbain studied at College of DuPage and the University of Wisconsin at Madison before transferring to Illinois, according to The Rhodes Trust. At Oxford, he plans to pursue a masters' degrees in diplomatic studies and public policy.</p><p>Michelle Du, a Virginia native studying at the University of Chicago, plans to pursue a master’s degree of science in social science of the internet, followed by a master’s degree in philosophy in socio-legal research, according to The Rhodes Trust. Du is finishing two degrees at the University of Chicago: a B.A. in law, letters and society and a B.S. in data science.</p><p>Over 3,000 students applied for the scholarship. Shahbain and Du were selected from 238 finalists, according to The Rhodes Trust.</p><p>With this weekend’s announcements, 3,738 Americans have received Rhodes Scholarships since the first U.S. class in 1904, representing 331 colleges and universities. Since women became eligible in 1976, 704 American women have received the award.</p>

entries.title: Blackhawks swap goalies with Rangers, trading Arvid Soderblom for Spencer Martin
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> found a new home for former backup goalie Arvid Soderblom on Sunday, six days after he cleared waivers.</p><p>The Hawks traded Soderblom to the Rangers in a goalie swap for veteran journeyman Spencer Martin.</p><p>Soderblom, 27, struggled throughout his three-plus years in the NHL with the Hawks, going 25-68-15 with an .885 save percentage. That number was .842 in his five appearances this season before his <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/08/blackhawks-backup-goalie-change-arvid-soderblom-waivers" >demotion</a>.</p><p>Martin, 31, historically has not been any better, though. In 73 career NHL games, he's 25-33-8 with an .881 save percentage. </p><p>He spent one full season (2022-23) as the Canucks' regular backup and has otherwise picked up those appearances in spot duty for several teams over the years, including seven times for the Rangers since the start of last season.</p><p>He has in played 270 career AHL games, as well, and was solid for the Chicago Wolves (the Hurricanes' affiliate) in 2024-25. He will report directly to the Hawks' affiliate in Rockford.</p><p>Both Soderblom and Martin are on expiring contracts, but Martin's $850,000 salary-cap hit is considerably cheaper than Soderblom's $2.75 million.</p><p>The Hawks now have an estimated $3.0 million in cap space, per PuckPedia, although they would have much more if they hadn't <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/01/08/blackhawks-sharks-trade-laurent-brossoit-nolan-allan-ryan-ellis" >acquired</a> retired defenseman Ryan Ellis' $6.25 million dead contract in January — back when they were more concerned about reaching the salary floor this season.</p><p>New Hawks backup goalie Drew Commesso hasn't started a game yet since his recall, but he'll likely get a chance sometime this week.</p>

entries.title: Bears' next opponent: Saints fall to the Panthers 20-17
entries.summary: <p>NEW ORLEANS — Chuba Hubbard gained 172 yards from scrimmage and ran for two touchdowns, and Ryan Fitzgerald's 54-yard field goal as time expired lifted the Carolina Panthers to a 20-17 victory over the New Orleans Saints on Sunday with the NFC South Division lead at stake.</p><p>The winning kick came after Saints cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry was called for a 30-yard pass interference penalty that gave Carolina the ball on the New Orleans 36-yard line with 21 seconds left.</p><p>Hubbard rushed for 92 yards, and also gained 80 yards on five catches for Carolina (4-5), which won despite committing 17 penalties for 152 yards. The Saints (3-6) by contrast, committed just three penalties, but the last cost them the game less than 30 seconds after Charlie Smyth had hit a 55-yard field goal to tie it at 17.</p><p>Carolina, which led 7-0 at halftime, was up just 10-7 when Alvin Kamara's 4-yard touchdown catch gave New Orleans a 14-10 lead with 3:49 left.</p><p>But Bryce Young used short passes to Hubbard for gains of 29 and 34 yards to set up Hubbard's second short TD run to put Carolina back in front with 1:49 left.</p><p>Tyler Shough, who was intercepted and lost a fumble during the game, drove New Orleans into position for Smyth's tying field goal.</p><p>Young finished 17 of 30 passing for 200 yards without a turnover. Shough was 25 of 35 for 187 yards. Saints rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson caught 11 passes for 80 yards.</p><p>But the Saints struggled to run the ball despite the return of Tavis Etienne from injured reserve. Etienne gained just 14 yards on eight carries and New Orleans finished with just 49 yards rushing. Kamara scored both Saints touchdowns, the first on a 3-yard run.</p><h3>Both teams squandered first-half scoring chances</h3><h3></h3><p>The Saints' first possession ended with Shough throwing an interception on fourth down at the Carolina 40, returned 41 yards by the Panthers' Devin Lloyd to the New Orleans 23.</p><p>Young was then stopped short by Carl Granderson on fourth-and-2 from the Saints 3.</p><p>In the second quarter, Fitzgerald missed a 48-yard field goal, keeping the game scoreless.</p><p>The Saints then marched to the Carolina 35, only to have Shough lose a fumble on a failed handoff.</p><p>After Carolina finally broke through on Hubbard's 2-yard touchdown run, the Saints drove to the Panthers 25, only to come up empty again when Audric Estime was stopped on fourth-and-1.</p><h3>Injuries</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Panthers:</b> Running back Jonathon Brooks (groin), offensive lineman Brady Christensen (hamstring) and safety Mike Jackson (groin) were not activated off injured reserve despite their recent returns to practice.</p><p><b>Saints:</b> Linebacker Pete Werner left the game in the first half with a hamstring injury.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Panthers:</b> Host Baltimore next Sunday.</p><p><b>Saints:</b> Visit the Bears at Soldier Field next Sunday.<br></p>

entries.title: Vikings beat Packers 30-10 in Kirk Cousins' return; Jordan Love is sacked 8 times
entries.summary: <p>GREEN BAY, Wis. — Kirk Cousins threw two touchdown passes to start his second stint with Minnesota and Levi Drake Rodriguez had two of the Vikings' eight sacks in a 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.</p><p>Cousins went 21 of 31 for 207 yards just five days after rejoining the Vikings, who acquired him from the Las Vegas Raiders at Tuesday's trade deadline.</p><p>The last time Cousins had played at Lambeau Field or suited up for the Vikings, he tore his Achilles tendon in a 24-10 Minnesota victory on Oct. 29, 2023. Cousins missed the rest of that season and then played for Atlanta from 2024-25 and Las Vegas the first half of this year.</p><p>Cousins rejuvenated an offense that had stalled under quarterbacks Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz, scoring 16 points or fewer in each of its last three games. He helped the Vikings snap a two-game skid as they beat the Packers for the fifth time in six meetings. And he reestablished his connection with top receiver Justin Jefferson, who had season highs in catches (nine) and targets (13) while finishing with 74 yards.</p><p>Minnesota (7-2) had scored 49 straight points against Green Bay (6-4) before Jordan Love's 32-yard touchdown pass to J. Michael Sturdivant in the third quarter cut the Vikings' lead to 20-7. The Vikings scored the final 29 points of a 39-22 season-opening victory.</p><p>Myles Price and Gavin Bartholomew each had their first career touchdown catches for Minnesota. Cousins threw a 38-yarder to Price in the first period and a 20-yarder to Bartholomew in the fourth.</p><p>Each of Minnesota's three touchdown drives included a third-and-long completion from Cousins.</p><p>Minnesota faced third-and-23 when Price caught a pass around the Green Bay 13, bounced off cornerback Brandon Cisse and ran into the end zone. Cisse injured his rib on the play and missed the rest of the game.</p><p>Cousins completed a 24-yard pass on third-and-15 to set up an Aaron Jones 1-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. Bartholomew's touchdown followed a 16-yard pass to Jefferson on third-and-12.</p><p>Love went 17 of 27 for 220 yards with a touchdown and an interception while facing constant pressure as the Packers lost for the second time in their last seven games. Love hadn't been sacked more than five times in any of his 56 previous starts, but the Vikings got their sixth sack Sunday on the first play of the second half.</p><p>Minnesota finished with its most sacks in a game since it had nine in a victory over Miami in 2018. The Packers hadn't allowed that many sacks since giving up nine in a loss to Arizona in 2015.</p><p>Virtually nothing went right for Green Bay.</p><p>The Packers entered the game with a plus-8 turnover margin that ranked second in the NFL, but they lost three fumbles — each leading to a Minnesota field goal — and Love was intercepted in the end zone by Harrison Smith.</p><p>An apparent Cousins interception got overturned after replays showed his knee was down before he threw the ball, and the Vikings scored a touchdown two plays later. Cousins was later picked off by Xavier McKinney, the safety's sixth of the season.</p><h3>Injuries</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Vikings:</b> OLB Bo Richter left with a foot injury in the first quarter. WR Jeshaun Jones hurt his shoulder in the third.</p><p><b>Packers:</b> CB Brandon Cisse (rib), WR/KR Skyy Moore (ankle) and WR Bo Melton (thight) left in the first half. Moore had been activated from injured reserve Saturday after missing four games with an ankle issue.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Vikings:</b> At San Francisco next Sunday night.</p><p><b>Packers:</b> At the Los Angeles Rams on Nov. 25.<br></p>

entries.title: Delays, cancellations dropping at Chicago's airports following Friday's ground stop
entries.summary: <p>Fewer delays and cancellations at Chicago's airports were reported so far on Sunday following Friday's nationwide ground stop.</p><p>As of mid-afternoon Sunday, O'Hare International Airport was reporting 450 delayed flights and 168 canceled flights, according to the flight tracking website FlightAware. That's a considerable drop from Saturday when the airport experienced 894 delays and 742 cancellations.</p><p>Midway International Airport saw similar improvements, according to FlightAware's data. As of Sunday afternoon, the airport had 147 delays and 37 cancellations. On Saturday, Midway reported 143 delayed flights and 76 canceled flights.</p><p>Air travel was thrown into chaos across the country Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare, nationwide ground stop. <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/transportation/2026/11/13/all-departing-flights-grounded-nationwide-due-to-faa-order" target="_blank" >Federal officials blamed</a> the country's aging air traffic control system for instability in air traffic control communications.</p>

entries.title: Judge Richard Posner eloquently defended the constitutional rights of all Americans
entries.summary: <p>Judges matter.</p><p>We've been reminded of that ever since Congress abandoned its role as a check on executive power, as the occasional court ruling slows the president's continual efforts to break the law, sometimes resisted even by his hand-picked minions on the U.S. Supreme Court who sometimes favor the Constitution over obedience to the whims of their sponsor.</p><p>Typically, Supreme Court justices issue the most important judicial opinions. But no voice on the high bench resonated louder than that of Richard Posner, who <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/11/11/richard-posner-longtime-federal-judge-and-prolific-university-of-chicago-legal-scholar-dies-at-87" >died last Tuesday</a>. And while he wrote eloquently on thousands of cases in more than a third of a century on the Chicago-based 7th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, one decision in particular affected the lives of millions of Americans: Baskin v. Bogin.</p><p>Penny Bogin was the clerk for Boone County, Indiana, a state that in 2014 still refused to recognize gay marriages performed in the 27 other states where it was legal.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-930000" name="module-930000"></a> <div class="RichTextSidebarModule-title">Opinion bug</div> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h2>Opinion</h2></div> </div><p>A U.S. District Court ruled the Indiana law violated the Constitution's guarantee of equal protection.</p><p>The matter, combined with a similar case in Wisconsin, seemed headed for the Supreme Court. But first the case had to stop at the 7th Circuit, where Posner cut it off at the pass.</p><p>Haters rarely care about the people they hurt beyond their intended targets. Posner quickly drilled down to who Indiana's law truly harmed the most, writing:</p><p>"Formally these cases are about discrimination against the small homosexual minority in the United States. But at a deeper level, as we shall see, they are about the welfare of American children."</p><p>Posner had a genius for plain language:</p><p>"Indiana’s government thinks that straight couples tend to be sexually irresponsible, producing unwanted children by the carload, and so must be pressured (in the form of governmental encouragement of marriage through a combination of sticks and carrots) to marry, but that gay couples, unable as they are to produce children wanted or unwanted, are model parents — model citizens really — so have no need for marriage. Heterosexuals get drunk and pregnant, producing unwanted children; their reward is to be allowed to marry. Homosexual couples do not produce unwanted children; their reward is to be denied the right to marry. Go figure."</p><p>Indiana's argument, "is so full of holes that it cannot be taken seriously. To the extent that children are better off in families in which the parents are married, they are better off whether they are raised by their biological parents or by adoptive parents. The discrimination against same-sex couples is irrational, and therefore unconstitutional. ... The harm to homosexuals (and, as we’ll emphasize, to their adopted children) of being denied the right to marry is considerable."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div Indiana's argument wasn't just refuted by Posner, as Esquire magazine noted, it was “tore into tiny pieces, lit on fire, and fed through a wood chipper.”</p><p>The Supreme Court declined to hear the case. Gay marriage became legal nationwide. In his ruling, Posner saw what would come next:</p><p>“Not that allowing same-sex marriage will change in the short run the negative views that many Americans hold of same-sex marriage.
